newsitem.title: BULGARIA: WESTERN FIRMS INTERESTED IN BULGARIA NATGAS NETWORK.
newsitem.headline: WESTERN FIRMS INTERESTED IN BULGARIA NATGAS NETWORK.

text.p: European Union's Energy Centre in Sofia said on Monday it would held a meeting for the development of Bulgaria's gas pipelines network and many western firms had shown great interest in it.

The centre said in a statement that the meeting, to be held in Sofia on Wednesday, was aimed at founding business contacts with West-European firms, interested in the development of the infrastructure of the gas pipelines' network.
Among the western firms are Italy's Tartini and Italgas Group, Greece's Asprofos and Pipelife Hellas and Netherland's Dansk Olie and Naturgas.

Bulgaria's gas monopolist Bulgargas and the Bulgarian-Russian joint gas stock company Topenergy, in which Russia's Gazprom holds a 50-percent stake, will present their project for the pipeleines' infrastructure at the conference.

Sofia is expected to decide on Topenergy's application for a concession for transit pipelines and other facilities in a month, Bulgaria's energy minister Roumen Ovcharov said on arrival from the venture's shareholders meeting, held on Friday in Moscow.
Topenergy, aimed at Russian gas sales to the Balkans, needs to increase the Bulgarian distribution system from 17 billion cubic metres to some 29 million cubic metres.
Bulgaria has a 2,000-km-long pipeline network, which includes 625-km transit pipelines. It is currently supplying Turkey and earlier this month started supplies for Greece.
Bulgaria has constructed and filled with gas a pipeline link with Macedonia and is waiting for it to complete construction works on its territory. Bulgaria plans to build a gas pipeline to Serbia.
